records.text: Monza - it is the epitome of speed, and not just for the Italian fans. The 124-year- old racetrack in the vast Royal Park of Monza has an aura for motorsport fans unlike almost any other place inthe world. When you turn off the main road onto Via Enzo Ferrari in this northern suburb of Milan and pass through the park gates, you are transported to another world. The historic steep bend, which you pass on the way to the Parabolica, has a gra- dient that is difficult to negotiate even on foot, and gives you just a glimpse of the courage it took to master this oval circuit in 1961 - the last year of Formula 1 - in those dainty and fragile Formula 1 cars. The fatal accidents of Wolfgang Graf Berghe von Trips in 1961, Jochen Rindt in 1970 and Ronnie Peterson in 1978 still cast ashadow over this circuit to this day. The Temple of Speed Yet at the same time, the fascination for the fastest track on the Formula 1 calen- dar - which has produced so many sto- ries and records - remains undiminished. Following an unprecedented slipstream battle, the top four crossed the finish line in 1969 within just 0.19 seconds of one another. Lewis Hamilton set the fastest F1 qualifying lap of all time here in the 2020 Mercedes F1 car, averaging over 264 km/h. Monza is rightly regarded as an Italian shrine, the temple of speed, and remains an absolutely magical place to this day. To mark this weekend’s Italian Grand Prix, we’ve taken the time to round up all the model cars currently available from the race’s long history. You’ll find a complete overview of the fascinating Formula 1 cars spanning more than 70 years on the following pages.
